title: Modification of the bitterness of caffeine
geographic_scope: International laboratory evidence; not Czech preference data

limitations: Abstract and publisher excerpts accessed; no finished founder drink tested

title: L-Theanine Elicits an Umami Taste with Inosine 5′-Monophosphate
evidence_type: primary human sensory and animal experiment
claims_supported: Concentration-dependent theanine taste; umami synergy in model system
limitations: Small panel; high model concentrations not validated RTD level

title: Suppression of Sourness by Theanine
publisher: Food Science and Technology Research / J-STAGE
claims_supported: Sourness change associated with pH and umami
limitations: Model acids and concentrations; not a universal caffeine masking result

title: Taste characterisation of green tea catechins
publisher: International Journal of Food Science and Technology
evidence_type: primary human sensory and mechanistic experiment
claims_supported: Specific EC ECG EGC EGCG profiles differ; concentration affects bitter/astringent intensity
limitations: Isolated model compounds not exact beverage extract

title: The taste of calcium and magnesium salts and anionic modifications

title: Trimagnesium Citrate
evidence_type: manufacturer technical specification and sensory claim
claims_supported: Anhydrous/nonahydrate identity; 16/12 percent magnesium; solubility distinction; neutral-taste claim

title: Suppression of bitterness by sodium: variation among bitter taste stimuli
claims_supported: Salt-bitter interactions vary by compounds
limitations: Simple solutions; research concentrations not proposed beverage doses

title: Sodium, but not potassium, blocks bitterness in simple model chicken broths
publisher: Journal of Food Science and Technology
